author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during their execution.
suggestedEngagement: Ask about the overcommit model they'd want: time-sliced vs. burstable cores — what would actually work for production agent workloads?
Share perspective on resource scheduling for agents: bursty, idle-heavy profiles make bin-packing hard; curious if he's seen any vendor get this right
Challenge/expand: this is the same problem container schedulers solved with cgroups + overcommit — what makes sandboxes structurally different that prevents the same approach?
